pageCache.pageTitle: Music - Chaddleworth St. Andrew’s & Shefford - C.E. Federated Primary Schools
pageCache.text:
Music
“Music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity.”
Music Curriculum Statement
At Chaddleworth St. Andrew’s and Shefford Federated Primary Schools, we believe that all our children should have access to the highest quality music education delivered by music experts (Berkshire Music Trust) as part of a broad and balanced curriculum.
Throughout their time at our school, all our children will be given the opportunity to sing, play musical instruments and create their own music. Our children will benefit from listening to the very best that every genre of music has to offer. The joy of listening to and participating in live performances will be experienced by all whilst in our school, creating memories that will last a life time.
Our carefully planned music curriculum ensures that all our pupils build their skills and knowledge, allowing them to perform, compose and listen with increasing insight.
We engage with specialist teachers from Berkshire Music Trust to deliver our music curriculum. All elements of the Early Years Framework and National Curriculum are covered and so much more, ensuring music is a key part of school life at Chaddleworth St. Andrew’s and Shefford Federated Primary Schools.
Weekly Pantomimus sessions as well as classroom activities ensure our EYFS and KS1 pupils are exposed to a range of musical genres and a wealth of opportunities to play, sing, compose, listen, perform and evaluate.
KS2 pupils receive specialist Music teaching for a minimum of 1 hour per week. They learn to recognise and name the interrelated dimensions of music – pitch, duration, tempo, timbre, structure, texture and dynamics – and use these expressively in their own improvisation and compositions.
Throughout KS2 all children have the experience of learning a musical instrument. The In2Music curriculum is a whole class instrumental teaching programme which allows children to apply their understanding of creating notes and practise reading basic music notation. They also learn how to compose, focussing on different dimensions of music, which in turn feeds their understanding when listening, playing or analysing music. There is a weekly choir available to all KS2 pupils and we do encourage and support those who have expressed an interest / talent for music to take part.
All pupils have the opportunity to express themselves musically in the above sessions as well as during singing worship, during performances such as such as our Harvest celebration, Nativity, Carol Concert, Easter performance and end of year performances. They experience live performances such as visiting the theatre at Christmas, participating in a production at our local theatre The Corn Exchange, joining Berkshire Music Trust for the Junior Music Festival, School Christmas Nativity and Carols and end of year school production performances.
We also offer small group tuition and 1:1 lessons in guitar, drumming, Ukulele, saxophone, flute and piano (these are subject to change as pupil interviews take place throughout the year to ensure that pupil voice is heard regarding the school’s music offer).
Berkshire Music Trust units of learning are tailored to the needs of our pupils and follow a spiral curriculum where previous skills and knowledge are returned to and built on enabling a more secure, deeper learning and mastery of musical skills. Progression through the units of learning allow children to learn concepts in an integrated, practical and exploratory way.
The impact of our Music curriculum and its implementation will lead to:
A record of those children who take part in additional music tuition, both inside and outside of school, is updated regularly throughout the year to ensure that we are aware of musical talent and encourage them to perform in assemblies and productions.
We are very proud of our musical achievements and have been awarded the Music Mark in recognition of our commitment to providing a high-quality music education for all children

pageCache.pageTitle: Worship - Chaddleworth St. Andrew’s & Shefford - C.E. Federated Primary Schools
pageCache.text:
Worship
Our school worship timetable brings us together each day through the school week to share reflective thought, song, prayer and celebration.
Collective Worship policy
Each Monday Whole School Worship we use a text, film or images to focus our thoughts and understanding linked to our Christian Values. Our book choices range from The Holy Bible, well known classic stories, to traditional tales to newly published texts. We also refer to the No Outsiders scheme that was introduced to our school in 2024 and it involves the use of age appropriate story books, created by Andrew Moffat MBE, who was nominated for the Global Teacher Prize.
No Outsiders has three core values:
- Respect for diversity through education in schools;- Commitment to community cohesion through understanding and acceptance of difference;- Promotion of dialogue to counter fear and hate in society.
You can find more information at the No Outsiders website.
Wednesday worship is led by Reverends Mike and Matt, again bringing our Christian Values to the forefront of our minds. Illustrated through Bible stories, questions, discussion, prayer and live music.
Our end of week Whole School Worship each Friday take a 'Sing and Celebrate' focus. We share our experiences of Christian Values in action and celebrate together. Children, and staff, are encouraged to celebrate with us their achievements and demonstrations of 'Living life in all its fulness', through new experiences and challenges that have been embraced, certificates and trophies that have been awarded and successes in and out of school.
Through the each week we also come together for class and then Key Stage worship where we are able to focus on current affairs through Picture News or Bible stories with a BIG question.
Our worship focus and resources are shared with families each week in our weekly newsletter to allow further thought and discussion at home.

Schools use the funds for pupils who have been registered for free school meals at any point in the last six years (known as ‘Ever 6 FSM’). We also receive funding for children who have been looked after continuously for more than six months, and children of service personnel.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art & Design - Chaddleworth St. Andrew’s & Shefford - C.E. Federated Primary Schools
pageCache.text:
Art & Design
Art and Design Curriculum Statement
Intent
At Chaddleworth St Andrews and Shefford Federated Schools we believe art and design is an important part of our broad curriculum and should stimulate children’s imagination and creativity. At our school the children will be given opportunities to experiment and create a variety of their own works of art. All children are given opportunities to develop their artistic skills as well as working with a variety of media. Throughout the years the children’s experiences will be enriched by finding out about famous artists and using their pieces of art to inspire the children’s own work as well as learning about the different styles used.
Implementation
Art will be taught every other half term and in a progressive way with children building on their skills year by year becoming more proficient in drawing, painting and sculpting skills. They will be given the opportunity to produce work that is creative and imaginative and will use sketch books to develop skills and record their ideas. Children will be given the opportunity to learn about a variety of artists with different styles and be given the chance to analyse and evaluate the work of the artists.
Class teachers will plan and teach the lessons using a variety of methods suitable for the age and class. Our whole curriculum is developed to enable all children, irrespective of background, ability or additional needs, to be given the chance to develop and be the best that they can possibly be.
Impact
By the time children leave Chaddleworth St Andrews and Shefford Federated Schools they will:
· Draw confidently from observation, memory and imagination.
· Have experimented with a variety of mediums.
· Use different styles and techniques to create their own works of art.
· Have a knowledge of a variety of artists and their styles.
· Be able to reflect on, analyse and critically evaluate their own work and that of others.
· To express their own opinions and feelings about different art styles or specific works of art.
· Recognise the joy of art – the creating, the feelings and the interests of the wide mix of art forms.

24th May 24
The children have made it to half term! What a busy few weeks we have had. This week we have started reading some animal poetry which the children have really enjoyed. We have been doing lots of rhyming in preparation for writing our own poems after half term. The highlight of our week was completing our sculptures that we have been working on this term. They were based on the "Dancing Grandmothers" sculptures by Stefani Morgante. This week we attached the clay heads to the paper bodies. Have a look at the photos below. We think you will agree - they look super!
We wish you all a lovely half term!

pageCache.pageTitle: 28th June 24 - Chaddleworth St. Andrew’s & Shefford - C.E. Federated Primary Schools
pageCache.text:
28th June 24
Once again, Kingfishers have had a very busy week! We have started looking at non-fiction texts in preparation for writing our own reports about an animal, year 1 and 2 both performed some wonderful music to each other in their music lessons, we cut out our animal puppets in preparation for adding the details next week and then sewing the pieces together the following week and finally we had an afternoon of science! What a busy week!
Our afternoon of science linked with "time" and involved the children carrying out an investigation to see if doing certain exercises made our hearts beat faster. We each took our pulse for one minute before we started the investigation. We then did a variety of activities. Each activity was done for thirty seconds and after each activity we took our pulses again for another minute. The children recorded their results after each exercise. We then talked about our results and what should happen to our body after doing exercise.
Have a look at the photographs of the children carrying out their investigation.
Have a lovely weekend!

pageCache.pageTitle: 3rd May 2024 - Chaddleworth St. Andrew’s & Shefford - C.E. Federated Primary Schools
pageCache.text:
3rd May 2024
Where have the past three weeks gone? The children in Kingfishers continue to be very busy. We have carried on thinking about sculpture in art, we have been planning our own versions of the story "Little Red Riding Hood", we have painted animals for science and much, much more! The children are currently enjoying their P.E. sessions outside where they have been developing their skills of throwing and catching through playing lots of games - have a look at the photo. The children are also getting very good at counting in French in their French lessons - well done Kingfishers!
Have a lovely weekend. Hopefully the sun will shine!
